Which features define published pancreas programs, and how do those programs
transfer to another measurement technology? This case study restores
published NMF programs as a view, ranks their features, summarizes activity by
cell type, then projects the fixed programs onto cells from a second platform.
It adapts Peter Carbonetto's
[single-cell Jamboree tutorial](https://stephenslab.github.io/single-cell-jamboree/pancreas_annotate.html).
The CEL-Seq2 cells originate from Muraro et al. (2016), assembled in the benchmark
of Luecken et al. (2022); source pages link the original studies.

## Prepare the attributed data

From a repository clone, run once outside package builds (about 86 MB downloaded;
preparation loads a roughly 640 MiB sparse matrix):

```sh
FLASHIER_UTILS_PANCREAS_DIR=~/pancreas-example scripts/run-r.sh .github/scripts/prepare-pancreas.R
```

The helper pins Jamboree revision `6cf9aa720cc16dc543e93b36d57bc1a85555860d`
and records source hashes. It selects 48 reference and 24 query cells while
retaining 14,528 genes. Set the same environment variable before running below.
Without the cache, examples are skipped; no download runs during a package build.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flashier.utils)
library(Matrix)
pancreas_dir <- Sys.getenv("FLASHIER_UTILS_PANCREAS_DIR")
have_pancreas <- nzchar(pancreas_dir) &&
  file.exists(file.path(pancreas_dir, "pancreas-worked-example.rds"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = have_pancreas, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r published-programs}
cache <- readRDS(file.path(pancreas_dir, "pancreas-worked-example.rds"))
source("restore-programs.R")
view <- restore_programs(cache$reference, cache)
factor_features(view, factor = "F4", select = "both", n = 5)[,
  c("feature", "estimate", "selection")]
```

`restore_programs()` restores published NMF coordinates through public native
initialization; it does not claim an independently fitted model. Largest effects
show contribution; distinctive effects depend on the selected competitors and
coordinate scaling. Biological labels need evidence beyond a ranking.

```{r group-activity, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
metadata <- cache$metadata[match(rownames(view$activity), cache$metadata$id), ]
metadata$sample <- as.character(metadata$id)
head(summarize_factor_activity(view, metadata, by = "celltype"))
plot_factor_activity(view, metadata = metadata, group = "celltype")
```

These cells have published cell-type labels but no donor identifiers. Summaries
are descriptive; technology is not a biological replicate.

## Transfer the fixed feature programs

`project_factor_activity()` keeps the reference effects fixed and estimates new
activities for the query cells.

```{r transfer}
projected <- project_factor_activity(view, cache$query_expression,
  sample_side = "rows", feature_scale = view$manifest$feature_scale,
  preprocessing = view$manifest$preprocessing, maxiter = 1000)
projected$reconstruction
stopifnot(identical(projected$representation$effects, view$effects))
```

Query counts use the reference library-size normalization and shifted-log rule.
Source effects stay fixed while query activities are re-estimated. Reconstruction
uses the same query observations used for activity inference, so it is fit
agreement, not held-out prediction. Query-set composition can change empirical
Bayes estimates; arbitrary row chunking is not exact. Transfer does not establish
biological conservation. See [Compare priors](compare-priors.html) for masked
prediction and [Advanced use](advanced-use.html) for coordinate uncertainty.
